input.query: apply for admission how to apply

results.response:
Applying to Indian River State College is free-ish of hassle and done entirely online through the River Application. Here are the steps:

1. Have your items ready: full legal name and date of birth, a personal email (not a school one), mailing address, cell phone, Social Security number if you have one, your high school info, any prior college transcripts, and a way to pay the application fee.
2. Go to the [apply page (apply.irsc.edu)](https://apply.irsc.edu/), click **Apply Now**, and select **River Application**.
3. Create your account with your personal email and a password, then fill out and submit the application. You can return any time to finish it, upload documents, or check your status.
4. Submitting a bachelor's (baccalaureate) application means paying a $30 non-refundable fee and sending official transcripts from your prior colleges.
5. To get our lower tuition rates, submit your Florida Residency Declaration (new to Florida, you can't establish residency just by enrolling for 12 months).

For most programs it's open to all who apply. After you're admitted, new students get an email within 3 business days with access to The River Portal, where you'll register for classes. Full details are in [Apply to Indian River State College](https://irsc.edu/admissions/apply/) and the [Admissions](https://irsc.edu/admissions/) page. Which program are you hoping to start? I can point you to the specific requirements.

Let me pull up the main dual enrollment page for a bit more detail.

Dual enrollment at Indian River State College lets a high school student earn college credit and high school course credit at the same time, so they can save both time and money. There are three tracks: **Academic**, **Career/Technical**, and **Early Admission** (for full-time enrollment after completing grades 9–11).

Here's how the path typically works:

1. **Meet with your high school counselor** to get your GPA and figure out which credits you still need to graduate.
2. **Apply to Indian River State College** and complete/upload the Dual Enrollment Program Agreement (Form 508) with your application.
3. **Submit placement scores** — take the P.E.R.T. or send in official ACT®/SAT® scores (no more than two years old).
4. **Register for classes** in the New River Portal — courses must be on the approved dual enrollment list, and you can't be enrolled in a dual enrollment class at the same time you're in high school.
5. **Pick up textbooks** — free through your school for public/charter students, or via the college bookstore for private and home school/PEP students.

There are also flexible locations: classes are offered on all Indian River State College campuses and at many high schools in Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, and St. Lucie County.

One important note: dual enrollment credit transfers to any public Florida college that offers a course with the same number, but the college can't guarantee how it will apply at out-of-state or private schools.

For the full details, approved course list, and dual enrollment calendars, see the [Dual Enrollment](https://irsc.edu/programs/special-programs/dual-enrollment/) page and the [Admissions – Dual Enrollment](https://irsc.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current/catalog/services-to-students/apply-for-admissions/admissions-dual-enrollment) catalog section.

3. **Payment plan** — If you'd like to spread the balance over monthly payments, the College offers a no-interest [FACTS Tuition Pay Plan](http://mycollegepaymentplan.com/irsc/) through Nelnet Corporation.

Full details, including residency rules and fees, are on the [Tuition & Fees](https://irsc.edu/admissions/tuition-fees/) page. input.query: Indian River State College Promise program who is eligible

results.response:
Let me pull the full eligibility details from the College's Promise page.

Here's who can qualify for the Promise Program at the College:

1. **Class of 2026 graduates** from a public, public charter, or approved private high school in **Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, or St. Lucie County**, or an eligible **in-district homeschool** graduate (homeschoolers need a River Affidavit Form + school district letter).
2. **U.S. Citizens or students lawfully present** in the U.S. As of July 1, 2025, DACA and undocumented students are no longer eligible.
3. A **minimum 2.0 high school GPA** (the one required for graduation).
4. **No financial-need or income requirements**, though you must complete a **FAFSA** each year. Bright Futures and other aid are applied first; Promise covers the remaining in-state tuition.

**Not eligible:** G.E.D.® holders, Florida Virtual School students, and PEP (Personalized Education Program) students.

Note that Promise covers **two years of in-state tuition only** (for AA/AS/AAS associate degrees) and does **not** pay for lab fees, books, or supplies. Full details, the [list of eligible schools](https://irsc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/promise-program-2025-approved-high-schools.xlsx), and staying-eligible requirements are on the [Promise Program page](https://irsc.edu/admissions/promise/). You can also reach the Financial Aid team through [The River Line](https://irsc.edu/student-resources/the-river-line/) if you have questions.
